title: The Qur'an in Abjad — Number, Structure, and Discernment

corpusAudit.countingNote: The whitespace-token count is for this exact file, not a universal canonical word count. Letter and total values are corpus- and method-dependent.

rules.feature: Graphic alif forms أ إ آ ٱ

claimsPolicy: This numerical-literary study is not a substitute for tafsir, Arabic philology, recitation, jurisprudence, or the living interpretive traditions of Islam.
Abjad cannot by itself prove doctrine, prophecy, divine intention, or a hidden code.
Numbers do not replace context or ethics; coincidence alone is not a miracle.
Digital roots are a modern reflection device.
Code claims are tested, not assumed.
Arithmetic identity proves arithmetic identity; a theological conclusion needs independent historical, linguistic, and interpretive support.
measured: phrase, verse, surah, title, and vocabulary totals
interpretiveControls: Long verses usually have larger additive totals; totals do not measure relative sanctity.
The literary imagery of a verse remains primary; Abjad adds an analytical layer rather than replacing language or context.

The observation that Qur'an 74:30 mentions nineteen, 114 = 6 × 19, and the conventional undiacritized Basmala has 19 normalized letters is reproducible arithmetic, not automatic proof of every modern nineteen-code claim.
